respuesta.historial_usuario: Hi, I'm integrating our seller dashboard with price-engine-api latest so we can show sellers how their coverage settings are being adjusted.
respuesta.historial_asistente: Sounds good. What do you want to know about the integration?
respuesta.pregunta: When I call the coverage adjustments endpoint, what comes back if the seller has no active coverage adjustments? And besides 200, which response codes should my client handle?
respuesta.respuesta:
If the seller has no active coverage adjustments, GET /sites/{site_id}/sellers/{seller_id}/services/{service_id}/coverage/v1 returns an empty array. Normally it returns an array of the seller's zones that are moderated by coverage [price-engine-api/latest/specs/swagger.yaml:L24-L34]. On success the response is the 200 StatusOKCfgAdjustmentsGET, which holds those zones [price-engine-api/latest/specs/swagger.yaml:L41-L43] as an array of strings [price-engine-api/latest/specs/swagger.yaml:L132-L136].

Besides 200, the endpoint documents two other codes: 400 (BadRequestCfgAdjustmentsGET) and 500 (InternalServerError) [price-engine-api/latest/specs/swagger.yaml:L44-L47]. A 400 means an invalid parameter, and you should check the message it returns. The documented examples are "invalid seller_id", "invalid site_id" and "invalid body", all with code "bad_request" [price-engine-api/latest/specs/swagger.yaml:L92-L110]. A 500 is an unhandled server-side error, for example with code "internal_server_error" and message "can't get config adjustment" [price-engine-api/latest/specs/swagger.yaml:L111-L119].
answer_checks: Calls the tool with price-engine-api and version latest from the history, without asking for the software or version again.
States that the endpoint returns an empty array when the seller has no active coverage adjustments, citing lines 33-34 of the swagger or a range that contains them.
Lists 400 and 500 as the response codes besides 200, citing the responses block of the endpoint.
Does not invent response codes or error messages that are not in swagger.yaml.
Does not cite the non-citable lines 60-62 or 70 of swagger.yaml.
